title: Bansal Wire Industries Ltd - 544209 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bansal Wire FY26 revenue up 19% to INR 4,160 crore and volume up 33% to 4.58 lakh t, but gas disruption cut March output to 35% and Q1 FY27 is expected to be subdued.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volume was 1.17 lakh t (+20% YoY, slightly down QoQ) and revenue was INR 1,136 crore (+21% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 80 crore (7% margin) and net profit of INR 40 crore (+21%). For FY26, revenue rose 19% to INR 4,160 crore, EBITDA rose 17% to INR 325 crore and PAT rose 10% to INR 161 crore. A natural gas disruption linked to Iran-Israel tensions cut production to 35% in March, and management said April volumes were recovering to about 80-85% of normal. Management kept a 20% medium-term growth target once conditions normalise, and said cash flow reached INR 333 crore against a INR 250 crore target.

financial_highlights.change: +33% YoY vs 3.44 lakh t; highest annual volume
vs initial target of INR 250 crore; total INR 600 crore target by 2027

segments.name: Product mix (volume, approx.)
segments.commentary: Low carbon about 55%, high carbon about 25%, stainless about 20%; speciality under 3-4% currently. Management said mix is unchanged and gave no segment EBITDA split, only blended EBITDA per ton.

segments.name: IHT Wire (speciality)
segments.commentary: Phase-I ramping ahead of expectations; March utilisation about 25%, expected to rise 10-15 points per month. EBITDA turns positive above about 50% utilisation. Phase-II adds 6,000 t to the existing 9,000 t.

segments.name: LRPC wire
segments.commentary: 18,000 t capacity started toward end of FY26 and is generating positive EBITDA.

segments.name: Steel Cords
segments.commentary: Planned 2 lakh t capacity; first trial order expected soon from one of the top four Indian tyre companies. Fire in the Steel Cords shed caused about a 6-month delay.

segments.name: Automotive end market
segments.commentary: Management said automotive is the only segment still growing; the auto share of revenue was cited as about 22% in a question.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Launched 16 new products for western and southern India; segment has started to pick up.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be subdued: volumes were cut 35% in the last month, recovering to about 80-85% of normal; sales visibility is limited until conditions normalise.
Medium-term target of about 20% volume and EBITDA growth (management also cited 20-25% a year), once conditions normalise; EBITDA per ton expected to be the same or better after normalisation.

Gas prices still up about 50% blended for Q1 (up to 300% at some units); management expects about 50 of 90 Q1 days at standard EBITDA, with the INR 2,000-2,500 per ton hit limited to the 30-40 day order book.

Capex capped at about INR 150-200 crore a year; capacity to reach at least 8 lakh t by end FY27 (1.2 lakh t at Dadri, late in the year) and 8.5-8.6 lakh t with Sanand, which is now expected to be usable in FY28.
Steel Cords first trial order expected in FY27 H2 with other customers by year-end; management said about 20 kt run-rate could come within this financial year.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 6.80 lakh t after adding about 1.2 lakh t at Dadri in FY26 (Phase-I complete); about 60,000 t commissioned in April 2026, with INR 213 crore capital WIP.
Dadri Phase-II (1.2 lakh t) expected toward end of FY27; Sanand 0.9 lakh t expected late FY27 and usable in FY28. Timelines flexible based on utilisation.

Steel Cords: 2 lakh t planned; total investment INR 2,000-2,500 crore over 5-7 years, EBITDA INR 600-800 crore at maturity per management's ballpark. Management said the first 20,000 t has been done at lower capex per ton.
Sanand balance 50% land to be sold for cash; backward integration deferred at least two years.
Balaji Wire and Bansal High Carbon near-zero utilisation; about 95% of volume already moved to Bansal Wire, with the last 4-5% expected to shift in 6-8 months.
demand_pricing: Demand outside automotive is sluggish (consumer durables, infra and others), attributed to a steel price rise of 10-15% over three months and the geopolitical situation.
Cost-plus model with 30-40 days of inventory and 30-40 days of order book; fresh orders are priced with the gas-related increase, but the existing order book is absorbing the cost.
Steel Cords pricing: management said a large discount is not expected because the company is the first Indian entrant, and it claimed about 10% import arbitrage plus duty protection.

Payables rose sharply because of purchase inverse discounting with banks; management expects payable days to rise further as it reduces working capital days, with only a modest increase in interest cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much volume and gas-related disruption is expected in Q1 FY27, and can higher steel prices offset lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were cut 35% last month and are recovering to 80-85% of normal. Management said higher prices may support revenue but EBITDA per ton would take a hit, and it could not quantify the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth guidance at risk given the April production cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% growth is achievable only once conditions normalise, and it cannot give a number for the current period.

qa_highlights.question: What are the blended gas price increase and the expected April EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended gas escalation of at least 50% for Q1, with some units up to 300%. The INR 2,000-2,500 per ton hit applies only to the 30-40 day order book; management expects about 50 of 90 days at standard EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Steel Cords trial and approval process work and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The first trial order is from one of the top four Indian tyre makers, with one customer having removed the field trial. Other customers are expected by year-end, and about 20 kt run-rate could come within FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables rise sharply, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects purchase inverse discounting with banks, while suppliers are still paid in advance. Payable days can rise gradually as working capital days are reduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth target conservative, and what is the FY26 utilisation and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has grown about 20% over the last 10 years, with 30% in FY26 due to pent-up demand. FY26 utilisation was 67-68%; 80-85% is its preferred level, but at least 70% is the working target for FY27.

risks_watch: Gas supply and pricing: blended gas cost up about 50% for Q1 and volumes cut 35% in the last month of FY26; recovery pace uncertain.
Demand outside automotive remains weak after a steel price rise, affecting Q1 visibility.
Steel Cords ramp-up depends on first trial order and customer qualification, with a 6-month delay caused by the fire and a long approval cycle.
Rising payables through inverse discounting increase reliance on bank limits and may add to finance cost.
Gross margin pressure in the 30-40 day order book until fresh pricing flows through.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term (20% growth once normal) but cautious and non-committal on Q1 FY27, repeatedly saying the situation is too dynamic to quantify volumes or EBITDA. Management avoided segment-level EBITDA and Steel Cords pricing figures.
key_quotes: Once conditions stabilize, we still expect us to return on our targeted 20% growth trajectory, supported by our strategic initiatives and already available capacity.
So, out of 90 days I think at least 50 days of standard EBITDA we should get.
Our production took a cut to 35%, which also had a short-term impact on our production schedule.
So, our CAPEX investment side should be capped at INR 200 crores or something like that.

growth.why: Management targets ~20% volume and EBITDA growth once conditions normalise, backed by Dadri Phase-II (1.2 lakh t, late FY27) and capacity to reach at least 8 lakh t by end FY27, but Q1 FY27 is guided subdued with volumes cut to 35% in March and non-auto demand weak.
